raw.details:
Dohyo is a head-to-head robotic pushing competition that puts power, traction, control, and strategy to the test. Two remotely controlled robots face off in a circular arena, with the objective of pushing the opponent completely outside the boundary or immobilising it. With intense 2-minute matches and knockout rounds, every push, manoeuvre, and positioning decision can determine the winner.

"Push. Outsmart. Dominate."

Details:

  • Category: Power
  • Duration: 2 Hours
  • Date: 17th October 2026
  • Time: TBD
  • Venue: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology
  • Mode: Offline
  • Team Size: 3–5 participants

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Open to all students.
  • Inter-college participants allowed.

Pre-requisites:

Competition-ready wireless-controlled robot complying with the specifications below:

  • Maximum weight: 8 kg
  • Maximum dimensions: 30 × 40 × 30 cm
  • Maximum voltage: 48V DC
  • Control: Wireless only
  • Operator: Single operator per match
  • Wired control: Not permitted
  • Emergency Stop/Kill Switch: Mandatory

Event Flow:

  • Each match will have a maximum duration of 2 minutes.
  • A match ends immediately if a robot is completely pushed outside the arena.
  • A robot may also win if the opponent becomes immobilised, defined as no wheel rotation for approximately 10 seconds.
  • If neither robot wins within the time limit, the judges will determine the result based on the applicable tie-break criteria.
  • For fewer than 7 teams, a Round Robin stage will be conducted, followed by the top 4 teams qualifying for the knockout stage.
  • For 7–10 teams, teams will be divided into 2 groups, with the top 2 teams from each group qualifying for the knockout stage.
  • In the knockout stage:
    • Semifinal 1: Rank 1 vs Rank 4
    • Semifinal 2: Rank 2 vs Rank 3
    • Final: Winners of the semifinals
  • In the group stage, points will be awarded as:
    • Win: 3 points
    • Draw: 1 point each
    • Loss: 0 points
  • Teams will be given 2 minutes of pit/repair time between rounds.
  • A tiebreaker match will be conducted if required to determine qualification or final standings.

Rules & Regulations:

  • The robot must comply with the specified 8 kg weight, 30 × 40 × 30 cm dimensions, and 48V DC maximum voltage limits.
  • Only wireless control is permitted. Wired control of the robot is strictly prohibited.
  • Only one operator is permitted to control the robot during a match.
  • Weapons, projectiles, explosives, pyrotechnics, flammable substances, high-pressure systems, or any mechanism designed to damage another robot or person are strictly prohibited.
  • The arena will be a circular platform with a diameter of 160 cm, featuring a clearly visible boundary and a flat, stable surface.
  • Robots must begin from their designated starting positions, approximately 20–30 cm apart, and must remain stationary until the official start signal.
  • Both robots must be fully inside the arena before the match begins.
  • Each robot must be equipped with a functional Emergency Stop/Kill Switch.
  • Any intentional interference with another team's wireless control system is strictly prohibited.
  • Robots will undergo weigh-in and verification before competition. Re-verification may be required after any in-competition repair or modification.
  • A robot pushed completely outside the arena boundary will be declared defeated.
  • A robot showing no wheel rotation for approximately 10 seconds may be declared immobilised and defeated.
  • Any unsafe operation or violation of the rules may result in a warning, penalty, or disqualification at the discretion of the event officials.
  • The decision of the event judges and marshals regarding match results, penalties, and disqualifications will be considered final.
